_meta.indication: ILARIS is an interleukin-1β blocker indicated for the treatment of Cryopyrin-Associated Periodic Syndromes (CAPS), in adults and children 4 years of age and older including Familial Cold Autoinflammatory Syndrome (FCAS) and Muckle-Wells Syndrome (MWS).

pivotal_trials.design: Three-part study: Part 1 was an 8-week open-label single-dose run-in to identify responders; responders who did not relapse by Week 8 entered Part 2, a 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled withdrawal phase; followed by Part 3 open-label treatment.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 9 to 74 years of age with the Muckle-Wells Syndrome (MWS) phenotype of CAPS.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint in the withdrawal period (Part 2) was the proportion of patients that had a disease flare (disease relapse or discontinuation prior to completing Part 2).
pivotal_trials.n: 35 patients enrolled in Part 1; 31 complete responders randomized into Part 2 (16 placebo, 15 Ilaris).
pivotal_trials.result: No disease flares in the Ilaris group (0 of 15), vs 13 of 16 (81%) in placebo; odds ratio 0, p < 0.01.

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of ACZ885 in Patients With Muckle-Wells Syndrome

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are nasopharyngitis, diarrhea, influenza, headache and nausea. In the Phase 3 CAPS trial (N=35): nasopharyngitis 12 (34%), diarrhea 7 (20%), influenza 6 (17%), rhinitis 6 (17%), nausea 5 (14%), headache 5 (14%). Injection site reactions occurred in 9% of patients in Part 1. Most serious risk is an increased risk of serious infections.
target_moa: Canakinumab is a recombinant human monoclonal anti-human IL-1β antibody of the IgG1κ isotype that antagonizes IL-1β by binding it and interfering with its interaction with the IL-1 receptor; uncontrolled overproduction of IL-1 is the pathogenetic mechanism of CAPS inflammation.
modality: mAb (recombinant human monoclonal anti-IL-1β antibody, IgG1κ)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened because canakinumab is a member of the IL-1 blocker class and the safety and efficacy data did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to already approved IL-1 blockers for CAPS.

description.text: Labeling update on vaccine use with canakinumab and Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule compliance; no new indication or population

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application proposes revisions to the labeling to include modification regarding available information about vaccine use with canakinumab. This supplement also provides for incorporation of information to the labeling to be consistent with the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLRR).

description.text: Expanded indication to include adults with active Adult-Onset Still's Disease (AOSD)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for expansion of the approved indication for the treatment of Active Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (SJIA) in patients aged 2 years and older, to include the new population of patients with active Adult-Onset Still's Disease (AOSD). Both, SJIA and AOSD, are referred to as Still's Disease. With the approval of this Prior Approval supplemental biologics application, canakinumab is indicated for the treatment of active Still's Disease, including AOSD and SJIA in patients aged 2 years and older.

description.text: Added indication for gout flares in adults in whom NSAIDs and colchicine are contraindicated, not tolerated, or inadequate, and repeated corticosteroids are not appropriate

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for the addition of a new indication: gout flares in adults in whom non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and colchicine are contraindicated, are not tolerated, or do not provide an adequate response, and in whom repeated courses of corticosteroids are not appropriate.

summary.text: Ilaris (canakinumab) received Orphan drug designation (December 18, 2008) and Fast Track (June 27, 2008) for CAPS, and was given a Priority 6-month review. It was approved first cycle on June 17, 2009 based on a single pivotal randomized withdrawal study in MWS without an advisory committee meeting, as it was the third IL-1 blocker approved and the second for CAPS.
